synopsis: Falsification optimizes scenario parameters to worsen measures such as time-to-collision, stopping margin or detection confidence, seeking reproducible failures and weak boundaries within the simulated space [f6835, f14146, f6841]. The recommended discovery campaign targets stopping boundaries, partial visibility, high closing speed, field-of-view edges and sensor degradation; weather tests should reproduce measured degradation rather than merely realistic appearance [f14155, f10937]. Discovery must remain separate from frozen estimation samples and regression testing: its failure fraction is biased by design, cannot represent an operational failure rate, and found failures should become logical scenarios or permanent regression tests [f133, f6842, f14157, f6949]. Failure-free searches do not prove failures absent, objectives can miss different failure types, and searches can exploit simulator artefacts [f6843, f6845, f6844]. Evidence includes on-road and aerospace work, but no off-road demonstration was found; VerifAI with Scenic reported up to a fivefold speed-up from parallel multi-objective falsification in 2021 [f14158, f6839]. The planning recommendation is to run inexpensive early falsification experiments before building major infrastructure [f10912].
